record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: In Precoloring Extension, the input is a graph G, a positive integer k, and a partial k-coloring of some vertices of G; the question is whether this partial coloring can be extended to a proper k-coloring of all vertices of G. What is the computational complexity of Precoloring Extension when the input graph is restricted to be a grid graph?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A grid graph is a finite induced subgraph of the infinite graph whose vertex set is $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$ and in which two vertices $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$ are adjacent if and only if $|x_1-x_2|+|y_1-y_2|=1$. (Equivalently, a grid graph is the Cartesian product $P_m \square P_n$ of two paths, or an induced subgraph thereof.)

For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $k$, a proper $k$-coloring of $G$ is a map $c:V(G)\to\{1,\dots,k\}$ such that $c(u)\neq c(v)$ whenever $uv\in E(G)$. A partial $k$-coloring of $G$ is a map $c_0:W\to\{1,\dots,k\}$ defined on some subset $W\subseteq V(G)$ such that $c_0(u)\neq c_0(v)$ whenever $u,v\in W$ are adjacent.

The Precoloring Extension problem takes as input a triple $(G,k,c_0)$, where $G$ is a graph, $k$ is a positive integer, and $c_0$ is a partial $k$-coloring of $G$, and asks whether there exists a proper $k$-coloring $c$ of $G$ such that $c(v)=c_0(v)$ for every vertex $v$ on which $c_0$ is defined.

Determine the computational complexity of Precoloring Extension when the input graph $G$ is restricted to be a grid graph.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an explicit open problem in a recent survey on graph-coloring problems for special graph classes by Paulusma, and web searches did not turn up any subsequent paper resolving the complexity of Precoloring Extension restricted to grid graphs. Related results are known (e.g., NP-hardness of precoloring extension on bipartite graphs, planar graphs, and unit interval graphs, and tractability on graphs of bounded treewidth with bounded number of colors), but the grid case appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes (Paulusma, survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 4: Determine the complexity of Precoloring Extension for grids.
status_evidence.claim: The complexity of Precoloring Extension on grid graphs is explicitly listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Precoloring extension - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Precoloring extension is NP-complete in general and remains so on several restricted graph classes; polynomial-time algorithms are known for graphs of bounded treewidth with a bounded number of colors.
status_evidence.claim: Survey-level sources discuss complexity on many restricted classes but do not record a resolution for grid graphs.
